brainlife.desc: FLAIR anatomical MRI volume (NIfTI): T2-weighted with CSF suppressed, sensitive to white matter lesions.
brainlife.name: neuro/anat/flair

original.desc: Fluid Attenuated Inversion Recovery (flair). The Flair sequence is similar to a T2-weighted image except that the TE and TR times are very long. By doing so, abnormalities remain bright but normal CSF fluid is attenuated and made dark. This sequence is very sensitive to pathology and makes the differentiation between CSF and an abnormality much easier.

brainlife.readme:
**Use for:** White matter lesion segmentation (e.g. LST-AI) together with a T1w. Synthesis of an MP-RAGE-like T1w from clinical FLAIR (SynthSR).

**Not for:** Cortical reconstruction or tissue segmentation that expects T1 contrast. Public sharing before defacing; lesions may reveal a diagnosis.

**BIDS:** anat/FLAIR (equivalent)

**Sharing:** Tier 3 (directly identifiable or traceable) by default.

**Apps:** Input to 7 Apps, output of 4 Apps.

Full record: https://github.com/brainlife/abcd-spec/blob/master/datatypes/neuro.anat.flair.json

identifying_risks: Face is recognisable in non-defaced images
Lesions can reveal a diagnosis such as multiple sclerosis
sharing_cautions: Deface before sharing outside a controlled project
Check for rare conditions in small samples
